feedback: No races have run yet, so this feedback rests on design reasoning rather than measured outcomes. In iteration 0 the main compensation I made was to set the sensor weights to the sign-correct, linear form (-2,-1,0,1,2), so the signal and steering direction agree with the contract. The 10 mm pitch over a 40 mm span gives a graded signal only while at least one sensor is partly on tape, so I could not confirm whether it saturates. If the next race shows line_loss_events above zero, or completion failing on the tighter bends, the likely cause is the sensor bar being too narrow for the 25 mm tape at high speed. In that case, widen the pitch to 15 mm (x = -0.03 to +0.03) before changing the footprint. If the race instead shows high steering_oscillation with few line losses, the 0.04 m forward offset is probably giving too much lag, so move the bar to y = 0.02 m. If the robot completes with low rms_error and fails only the time target, the chassis is the limit, so try a smaller wheel_track or a higher wheel_radius for more top speed.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is above 0 or the robot leaves the line on bends, widen sensor pitch from 10 mm to 15 mm (x = -0.03 to +0.03, y = 0.04). No race has tested this yet; it is based on the 25 mm tape and 12 mm footprint.
If steering_oscillation is high while line losses are low, reduce forward offset from y = 0.04 to y = 0.02 m to cut lag. No race evidence yet; this follows the 0.04 m lookahead hypothesis.

If the robot completes but progress reaches 0.995 too slowly for 3 s, try wheel_radius 0.035 with wheel_track 0.10 for more top speed. No race evidence yet; this follows the 1.5 m/s average requirement.
